name: Ligation buffer
components: Tris-HCl 50 mM; KCl 100 mM; MgCl2 10 mM; DTT 1 mM. ATP is charged into the reaction rather than into this buffer and its concentration is contested (P-LIG-ATP, Q-040); PEG is not used in the demonstrated route and is struck
storage: 2-8 C prep; enzyme cold chain - but see notes: 2-8 C is NOT a no-growth condition and the setpoint within it is a real decision (Q-043)
notes: COMPOSITION FILLED 2026-09-25, and the correction is instructive: this row said 'concentrations TBD', left pH blank, and instructed 'Do NOT invent concentrations' - while SRC-ALMAC-2023, which this register already marked full-text-read, prints the composition in its Methods. Verified verbatim against the document: 'reaction buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, 100 mM KCl, and 10 mM MgCl2, prepared in nuclease free water)' and, separately, the extract 'was resuspended in reaction buffer containing 1 mM dithiothreitol (DTT)'. So the caution was correct in principle and MIS-TARGETED in fact: a gap was registered where the evidence was already inside a source read in full. It was a partial gap, not the worst defect in the register - the pH and four concentrations were missing, nothing more. SCALE AND SYSTEM THAT MUST TRAVEL: 96-well screening and bench-to-1 L, fully modified siRNA blockmers carrying phosphorothioate linkages and GalNAc, with an RNA-ligase/PNK cell-free extract. The anneal is run in this same buffer at 0.2 mM (2x final per blockmer) for 15 min at 65 C (P-LIG-ANNEAL-T, P-LIG-ANNEAL-HOLD). TWO CONSEQUENCES CARRIED ELSEWHERE. The 10 mM MgCl2 is a divalent cation that binds the polyanion and will not simply diafilter out, so it can block impurity clearance in UF/DF (R-014, IMP-DIVALENT, SRC-GRONKE-2023) - and chelating it at the quench would convert it into the net-negative Mg-EDTA complex, pointing it the RIGHT way through the membrane (inference, ours; C-014, Q-059). The 1 mM DTT is a copper reductant and a metal-chelator tolerance problem: it disqualifies the BCA total-protein assay by the vendor's own manual and it is the reducing agent that IMAC resins based on IDA tolerate worst, which matters because the one demonstrated immobilised route uses Ni-IDA (Q-061, C-012). STORAGE IS NOT A NO-GROWTH CLAIM: cardinal minimum growth temperatures for the common panel are 4 C for Bacillus cereus, Bacillus subtilis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa and 7 C for Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus (SRC-BPI-HOLDTIME-2025), so at 2-4 C nothing in that panel grows while at 8 C most of it does. 'Jacketed chilled hold or not' is therefore really 'setpoint below 4 C or not', and only the lower choice buys a mechanistic growth-arrest argument (Q-043, R-009, UT-CHILL).

name: Ligation stop solution - analytical sampling only
use: Terminating a WITHDRAWN ALIQUOT of the ligation so it can be analysed. NOT a process unit operation and not a batch-termination step: nothing retrieved terminates a modified-siRNA ligation at process scale (Q-059, Q-060)
components: EDTA 50 mM + Tris-HCl 10 mM at pH 7.5, added 1:1 by volume into the reaction, so 25 mM EDTA and 5 mM Tris final
storage: Ambient; made up as a 1x stock and added by volume at the sampling point
notes: REGISTERED 2026-09-27, with the analytical-scale caveat that is the whole reason this is a buffer row and not a unit operation. THIS IS THE ONLY CHEMICAL STOP ON A LIGATION IN THE WHOLE SOURCE REGISTER, verbatim: 'A control reaction was prepared by addition of 25 ul of a stop solution containing 50 mM EDTA and 10 mM Tris-HCl at pH 7.5 before ligase addition. The ligation reactions were then incubated at 37 C with reactions halted at 15, 30, 60, 120, 240 and 480 min by addition of 25 ul stop solution.' Re-retrieved 2026-09-27 via the Europe PMC REST service. SCALE, WHICH DISQUALIFIES IT AS A PROCESS STEP: reactions are 25 ul, the probes are 2.5 nM, the substrate is UNMODIFIED DNA on an mRNA splint, and the whole point of the series is a qPCR time course. The stop solution is sampling hardware. THE OTHER CHEMICAL STOPS ARE NOT ON LIGATIONS AT ALL. SRC-NEB-WO2023173098 has three recipes - '2x Quench Solution (20 mM EDTA, 2% SDS)', '2 ul of 30 mM EDTA and heating at 75 C for 5 min', and '10 uL 50 mM EDTA with 0.7 % Tween-20' - and every one of them stops a CAPPING or POLY(A) TAILING reaction feeding capillary electrophoresis or LC-MS. SRC-ALMAC-2023 quenches with methanol into UPLC, and its two figures ('100% v/v' in the PNK screen, '1 volume' in the RNAL screen) are one recipe in two units on two different screens rather than two data points. So the register can state what an analytical quench is and cannot state what terminates the batch: Q-060 stays blank and Q-059 stays open. THE CHELATION CONSEQUENCE ALREADY CARRIED: EDTA converts BUF-LIG's 10 mM MgCl2 into the net-negative Mg-EDTA complex, which points it the RIGHT way through the UF/DF membrane (C-014, IMP-DIVALENT, R-014) - an inference of ours, and one reason a chelating stop is attractive at process scale if anyone ever measures one. RETRIEVAL HAZARD: the paper prints 'Tris-HCl' with an EN DASH (U+2013), so a quote transcribed with a hyphen will not string-match, and PubMed Central served a reCAPTCHA page to every direct route tried.

name: Diafiltration exchange buffer
use: UF/DF buffer exchange - the last chance to decide what enters the evaporator
storage: 2-8 C or ambient; no reason to chill a salt-free matrix beyond the product's own hold requirement (Q-043)
notes: COMPOSITION FILLED 2026-09-27 as an estimate, not as a fact, and the provenance is the point: this row read 'Exchange from reaction salts toward final matrix - composition TBD' under provenance=assumption, which told a reader the project had no view. It has a view and can defend it; what it does not have is a document stating it. R-005 is the constraint that does the work - evaporation concentrates whatever is left in solution into the powder - and it applies to a replacement BUFFER exactly as much as to the reaction salts, which is the step the old 'toward final matrix' wording skipped. See BUF-FINAL for the excipient, which is a separate decision (Q-038), and Q-020 for the diavolumes. SCALE AND SYSTEM: no oligonucleotide UF/DF buffer-exchange endpoint has been retrieved at all (Q-035, Q-036, Q-041); the approved-label evidence is about a FORMULATED DRUG PRODUCT in a vial, not about a diafiltration endpoint, and the transfer is ours.
est_value: Water for injection, with no added salt, no Tris and no divalent cation - the diafiltration target is a matrix that leaves nothing behind when it evaporates, not a replacement buffer
basis: The approved record says a duplex siRNA does not need a buffer to sit in: SRC-SIRNA-LABELS reads six US labels and one PMDA summary, and four of the seven products carry NO weighed excipient at all at 160-200 mg/mL - Givlaari and Leqvio are verbatim 'formulated in Water for Injection' with sodium hydroxide and/or phosphoric acid only for pH adjustment. So the liquid matrix is a free choice, and the thing that constrains it is downstream: whatever is dissolved here is concentrated by the evaporator and then dried into the powder, which is why the reaction salts have to leave rather than be swapped for different ones. The 10 mM MgCl2 of BUF-LIG is the specific case - a divalent cation bound to a polyanion does not simply diafilter out (IMP-DIVALENT). Q-020 stays open: this says WHAT to exchange into and not how many diavolumes it takes, and the two are independent. Q-038 stays open too - whether the excipient joins here or after the evaporator is a different decision and this estimate deliberately does not make it.
falsifier: A melting-temperature or aggregation measurement on THIS duplex at the diafiltration endpoint ionic strength showing it destabilises without counterions - the one physical reason a salt-free target would be wrong, and the reason it is an estimate rather than a conclusion. A measured Tm drop that crosses the process hold temperature forces a counterion into the matrix and this row is rewritten. Equally: any spray-dryable-matrix study requiring a buffer salt for powder integrity.

name: Final spray-dry matrix
notes: COMPOSITION FILLED 2026-09-27 as an estimate. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT, UNCHANGED: must be spray-dry compatible so evaporation does not concentrate Tris/Mg/NaCl into the powder (R-005). The glass-forming excipient is a DRYING and POWDER-PROPERTY aid, NOT a chemical stabiliser: approved siRNA products are stable at 160-200 mg/mL in essentially pure water and four of seven carry no weighed excipient (SRC-SIRNA-LABELS, F-024). So the ratio is set by what the DRYER needs, not the molecule (Q-021). WHAT CHANGED 2026-09-27: the row previously wrote 'Glass-forming excipient (trehalose/sucrose?) + minimal/volatile buffer - TBD' into the composition column under provenance=assumption. Two defects in one cell. The question mark after 'trehalose/sucrose' was an invented identity wearing a hedge - nothing retrieved names either sugar for an oligonucleotide powder - and 'minimal/volatile buffer' contradicted the label evidence this very row cites, which is that four approved products carry no buffer at all. The estimate now says only what can be defended, which is what the matrix must NOT contain, and the identity is left where it belongs, in Q-021. GAP still pending stream F/G.
est_value: One glass-forming excipient in water for injection and nothing else - no buffer salt, no chloride, no divalent cation. The excipient's IDENTITY and its ratio to API both stay gaps (P-EXCIPIENT-RATIO, Q-021)
basis: What this estimate claims is what is ABSENT from the matrix, and that part is defensible from the record. SRC-SIRNA-LABELS: four of seven approved siRNA products carry no weighed excipient at 160-200 mg/mL in essentially pure water, so the active substance needs nothing added for chemical stability in the liquid state - any solid in the dried matrix is there for the DRYER and the powder. R-005 then rules out carrying Tris, magnesium or chloride through evaporation, because evaporation concentrates them into the product rather than removing them, and a spray-dried powder has no rinse step afterwards. What the estimate deliberately does NOT claim is the excipient itself: no dried siRNA product has ever been approved, so no identity and no ratio transfers, and naming trehalose or sucrose here would be inventing the one number Q-021 exists to hold open. Q-021 stays open on the ratio and the identity; Q-038 stays open on where the excipient is introduced.
falsifier: An approved or published siRNA formulation in which a buffer salt or chloride is present for CHEMICAL stabilisation of the active rather than for tonicity or pH adjustment - that would make the salt-free target wrong rather than merely minimal. Or a spray-drying study on an oligonucleotide showing the powder requires a buffered matrix for glass formation or for residual-moisture control.

name: TFF membrane cleaning caustic
use: Recirculated caustic clean of the UF/DF cassettes between batches - a DIFFERENT chemistry from every other unit operation, which is ISPE's own instruction and not our preference (SRC-ISPE-WIENCEK-2006)
components: NaOH 0.1 N - 0.5 N (0.1-0.5 M), 25-50 C, 30-60 min recirculated, then a water flush. Both endpoints are printed by ONE document and the span is an inherited convention rather than two measurements - see notes and Q-075. The 100-hour cumulative exposure cap travels WITH this recipe
ph: 13 - the arithmetic pH of 0.1-0.5 N NaOH, printed as 'pH 13' for the same solution by SRC-CYTIVA-CFF and MEASURED at approximately 13 by SRC-ATWELL-2017. The 'pH 10 - 11' printed beside this row in SRC-MILLIPORE-PELLICON3 is the hypochlorite figure standing next to a caustic row and is deliberately NOT carried
storage: Made up fresh per clean, single-use to drain. Do not confuse with the membrane's STORAGE agent, which is 0.1 N NaOH for up to one year at 2-8 C in the same document - a different duty with a different exposure budget
notes: REGISTERED 2026-09-27. It is a fact in the only sense that matters here - a vendor prints it - and three qualifications travel with it or it is misread. (1) ONE SOURCE AT BOTH ENDS, AT CONVENTION LEVEL. ENV-018 audits the endpoints and returns one_source_both_ends, not two_independent: the 0.1 N and 0.5 N ends are two ends of one printed span in one document. The same four numbers reappear in SRC-CYTIVA-CFF in M rather than N, attached to sanitization rather than cleaning, and do NOT reappear in SRC-CYTIVA-HF, which circulates a 0.5 N point at 50 C for an hour. Numbers that survive a unit change, a membrane change and a change of unit operation are an industry convention; Q-075 holds that open. (2) THE VENDOR DISCOURAGES ITS OWN TOP END AND CAPS TOTAL EXPOSURE, verbatim: 'There is an initial NWP decline in Pellicon 3 Cassettes after initial exposure to 0.5N NaOH. Better membrane life has been observed at lower concentrations. Total exposure time must not exceed 100 hours.' No Cytiva document carries a cumulative budget, so merging the two sources would silently drop it. (3) THE TEMPERATURE ENDS CONFLICT ACROSS VENDORS. This row's 25 C low end is refused by SRC-CYTIVA-HF - 'Cleaning at room temperature (i.e., 20 C) is not recommended', preferring 50 C and refusing above 60 C - while SRC-CYTIVA-CFF's own Table 3.1 prescribes 20 C for a hypochlorite/caustic blend. Two Cytiva documents disagree and neither cites the other. SCOPE THAT MUST TRAVEL: the chart is headed 'Organics, Biofilms, Biopolymer, Proteins and Polyphenolic' - a protein/biopolymer soil. Our soil is a fully modified polyanion plus extract protein in Tris/KCl/MgCl2/DTT, which nobody has cleaned off a cassette (Q-074), and the caustic will not degrade the product (see BUF-CIP), so the duty is removal measured analytically. Cytiva states the transfer limit outright: 'Optimization of the procedures in terms of chemical concentration, recirculation time, temperature and pH will typically be performed on a case-by-case basis.'

name: Stainless-equipment caustic CIP wash
use: Recirculated caustic wash for every NON-membrane unit operation - buffer prep, the ligation vessel, clarification, the evaporator and the dryer - delivered by the CIP skid
storage: Batched on the CIP skid from concentrate and sent to drain after the wash; whether any circuit re-uses a wash is part of Q-074 and is not assumed here
notes: REGISTERED 2026-09-27 as the first educated estimate in this repository, and the first row of any kind to carry provenance=judgement. TWO ROWS, NOT ONE, AND THE SPLIT IS QUOTED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: SRC-ISPE-WIENCEK-2006 says 'TFF membranes usually require cleaning chemistries and temperatures that are different than all other unit operations. Establishing specifications for each unit operation may minimize the need to test multiple CIP chemistries at the production scale.' So this row covers the vessels and BUF-MEMBRANE-CLEAN covers the cassettes. THE PRODUCT IS NOT DESTROYED BY THIS WASH, AND THAT IS A MECHANISM CLAIM AND NOT A CLEANING ARGUMENT. Our product is a fully modified duplex (SRC-ALMAC-2023) and SRC-EGLI-2023 states that 2'-modification 'affords chemical stability in that it precludes 2'-OH-mediated strand cleavage' - so a residue should be expected to SURVIVE caustic rather than be degraded by it. The inference that was tried and dropped is the next step: nothing in cleaning validation requires a residue to be chemically destroyed, so 'it resists caustic' neither raises nor lowers the cleaning duty, which is removal to an analytically measured limit. The review never uses the word alkaline, caustic or hydroxide - zero occurrences, measured - and no primary source has exposed a fully 2'-modified siRNA to caustic cleaning conditions. WHAT THIS ROW IS NOT: it is not a residue limit. Q-047 asks what the HBEL/PDE is and P-HBEL-DS stays blank; a recipe and a limit are different quantities and both gaps are open. THE SOIL IS THE TRANSFER PROBLEM: the one measured caustic threshold behind this estimate was taken on brewery soil (yeast and protein on stainless, cold), and ours adds a polyanion that caustic will not cleave and a divalent cation bound to it.
est_value: NaOH 1% w/v (0.25 M), 30-60 min recirculated, ambient to 50 C
basis: CONCENTRATION - the strongest leg. 1% w/v NaOH is the only caustic strength anyone has measured a cleaning ENDPOINT against on a protein-bearing soil on stainless: SRC-ATWELL-2017 ran 90 full-factorial coupon cleans and found, verbatim, that 'NaOH needs to be at least 1% w/v for the clean to be effective' and that above 1% w/v 'there is no additional cleaning benefit'. 1% w/v is 0.25 M, which sits inside the 0.1-0.5 M span both TFF vendors print (SRC-MILLIPORE-PELLICON3, SRC-CYTIVA-CFF) and on its lower half - the direction Millipore's own 'better membrane life has been observed at lower concentrations' points. CONTACT TIME: 30-60 min is what both vendor documents allow for a caustic recirculation, and one caustic step of that length fits inside the 'two to four hours' SRC-ISPE-WIENCEK-2006 gives for a whole optimised caustic/acid cycle. TEMPERATURE IS THE WEAK LEG AND IS GIVEN AS A SPAN FOR THAT REASON, NOT FOR CONVENIENCE: SRC-ATWELL-2017 cleaned effectively at ambient 'consistent with industrial operation', while SRC-CYTIVA-HF says 20 C 'is not recommended' and prefers 50 C, refusing above 60 C - and neither system is ours. NOT PART OF THE BASIS, NAMED HERE SO IT CANNOT BE MISTAKEN FOR ONE: SRC-ISPE-WIENCEK-2006's '1% by volume' is a waste-arithmetic placeholder introduced by the word Assume and attached to no soil, no temperature and no contact time; that it agrees with the measured figure to one significant figure is a coincidence and is treated as one. Q-074 is not closed by any of this: nothing has cleaned OUR soil, and until a coupon study does, this is an estimate.
falsifier: A coupon cleanability study on the real soil - ligated fully modified duplex plus RNA-ligase/PNK extract protein in Tris/KCl/MgCl2/DTT, dried onto 316L - that leaves residue above the carryover limit after 1% w/v NaOH for 60 min at 50 C. That falsifies the concentration upward. The estimate is equally falsified DOWNWARD: the same study coming back clean at 0.1 M would make 1% w/v needlessly strong and wasteful of both caustic and rinse water. SRC-ISPE-WIENCEK-2006 names the experiment: 'Cleanability studies utilizing soiled coupon testing may identify the proper cleaning chemistry and temperature at a bench top scale.'
